observed.facings.png: Three grounded facings of the owner-kept reference body on a checkerboard, all at one scale. South: a heavy, front-facing grey-ochre beast with tall tufted lynx-like ears, narrow fierce eyes, a pale chest, white-and-slate chevron bands on the flanks, a big bushy banded tail off to the left, and large claws. East: a long, low side profile with a heavy chest, slate and fog-white bands along the flank, a whiskered fierce head with swept-back ear tufts, a long banded tail and large hooked claws. North: the rear, with ear tufts at the top, the back and haunches showing bands, and the tail hanging down the middle. No face is visible.
observed.south.png: The grounded south at full resolution. Front view, face to the camera, hunched heavy body, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: The grounded east at full resolution. Side profile walking right, deep chest, banded flank fur fold, prominent claws, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The grounded north at full resolution. Rear view with the tail centred and ears behind, no eyes, clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the grounded south sits about one cell tall beside the vanilla human, roughly half the human's height. At 32 px/cell it reads as a small grey spiky shape, a bit bigger than the rat.
observed.flight_1.png: East flight frame. A long, slim, flattened glider stretched horizontally with its head right. A membrane runs from the forelimb to the hindlimb, banded fog-white and slate. All four limbs reach out at the corners with dark hooked claws. A bushy pale-tipped tail trails left. The head has swept-back ear tufts and a fierce look. The body is narrow and streamlined, with no deep keel visible. Clean alpha.
observed.flight_2.png: Looks identical to flight_1 at this resolution. I cannot see any membrane-edge billow.
observed.flight_3.png: Looks identical to flight_1/2. The billow at 1.16 is not visible to me.
observed.flight_5.png: North flight frame. A dorsal view from behind and above. The body is a narrow grey spine with ears at the top. A wide rectangular membrane is spread flat to both sides, banded slate and fog-white, with clawed hands and feet at its four corners. A bushy tail with a white tip hangs down toward the camera. No face. It reads close to a plan view of the back, though the membrane is somewhat foreshortened vertically.
observed.flight_9.png: South flight frame. A front view with the head at the centre and the tail rising up behind it, and a membrane spread wide to both sides with white and slate bands and clawed limbs at the corners. The face is a chipmunk/flying-squirrel face: large round dark glossy eyes, bold dark-and-white facial stripes, a small pink-brown nose, and short rounded ears with small tufts. It is unlike the grounded south's narrow-eyed, tall-eared, heavy-browed face. The body looks slim. Clean alpha.

reply.image_seen: Images 1–4 show grounded front, side and rear references with tall pointed ears, heavy limbs and folded banded membranes; image 5 shows scale beside a human; images 6–8 show three east-facing gliding frames with extended legs and broad striped membranes.

concerns.evidence: The attached flight frames are east views, with swept pointed ears and a long muzzle consistent with the grounded east reference. South flight frames 9–12 are absent, so their alleged change in head anatomy cannot be checked.
No south flight face is attached. The visible east flight heads have narrow profiles and pointed ears; they cannot establish whether the south frames have glossy round eyes or a cute striped mask.

The east flight torso appears shallower than the grounded side reference, but the broad membrane overlaps its flank and the legs are extended into a glide. These views do not clearly distinguish an absent deep chest from pose and membrane coverage. North and south flight frames are missing.

The alleged Earth flying-squirrel appearance concerns an unattached south flight view. The visible east frames retain the pointed head, swept ears, clawed limbs and slate-and-white membrane bands, but cannot settle the south-view concern.

request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite, the shirrel, in flight with its gliding membranes spread, on a transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, matte textured fur, clean dark outline. The shirrel is a cat-sized, heavy-bodied glider of the Leaning Scrub, STORM-GREY: charcoal body, with a full body-length gliding membrane stretched from wrist to ankle on each flank, banded slate and fog-white like weather unrolled. The torso is heavy and deep-chested: in the east view a visible deep keel under the chest, in the north view (rear, seen from behind, back and haunches with eyes hidden) and the south view (front, eyes toward the viewer) a broad thick body between the two membranes. The head matches the grounded shirrel sprite exactly: tall swept tufted lynx-like ears, narrow fierce wary eyes under a heavy brow, a grey-ochre face with pale cheek bands. Strong, prominent climbing claws at the wrists and ankles, splayed at the membrane edges. Same palette, body plan and head in every frame, so the flying shirrel reads as the same alien storm-grey beast as the grounded sprite.
